Hi Elina / Tom —

Thanks again for the call last week. Per our discussion, I’m sending a concrete amendment we can add to your existing hosted contract to support the increased Q3 traffic pattern you described. High level:

- Monthly committed tokens: increase from 120M -> 240M (effective 2026-07-01)
- Quarterly burst pocket: 200M tokens available for 90-day bursts, billable if used beyond committed volume at the negotiated overage rate
- Temporary soft-throttle grace: two-week buffer on new commit enforcement during cutover

Attachments: RetailNova_SOW_Q3-2026.pdf (proposal) and a usage export for May to show baseline.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review with procurement and ops (I’ve cc’d Karthik for operational impact)
2) If ok, I’ll send a formal amendment (DocuSign) and a one-page summary for your legal/finance team
3) Target go-live: 2026-07-01 to capture Q3 peak

Open to adjusting the burst size if you expect a higher peak — happy to run quick cost estimates.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Tom — thanks for the questions. Quick answers from an ops/runtime perspective: 

1) Invoice cadence: increases to the committed tier will be reflected as a single line-item "Hosted API committed tokens (monthly)" on the monthly invoice. We can mark the PO description string for you so procurement can map it to your ledger — please share the exact PO wording and we'll echo it in the invoice metadata.

2) Burst alerts: yes — we can configure automated email + Slack alerts at 70% and 90% of the burst pocket. Additionally we expose token-level dashboards (per-route) in the Console; we can give RetailNova read-only access for the cutover period.

3) SLA & credits: p95 latency target for the committed tier will be 350–450ms depending on route mix. We have a standard SLA clause that ties service credits to monthly availability and p95 latency regressions. I attached Commit_Amendment_v2.docx which includes the proposed SLO language and soft-throttle guardrail wording (two-week ramp with throttling thresholds and auto-fallback to current commit if anomalies detected).

Operational notes: during the first 14 days post-cutover we will keep aggressive KV cache priming and higher batching windows to reduce token costs while meeting latency goals. That’s why we recommended the temporary grace window.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with your ops if helpful — Marissa / Stephanie can join to discuss onboarding and invoice mapping.

—
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
